code-integration-reviewer.exactClaim: Codebase Memory still reserializes a live parsed external result in the transport adapter, so the generic live-result serialization was relocated rather than removed.
code-integration-reviewer.recommendedCorrection: Remove JSON.stringify(value.result), preserve serialized text through the process boundary, and add production-path oversized/valid-result coverage.

test-quality-reviewer.exactClaim: The production transport still serializes a parsed upstream result, while the oversized regression bypasses that transport and does not prove the end-to-end boundary.
test-quality-reviewer.recommendedCorrection: Add a CodebaseMemoryProcessTransport regression for oversized UTF-8 output before JSON.parse and normalization.

security-reviewer.exactClaim: The process transport still serializes a parsed live result object before returning it to the generic serialized boundary and could invoke attacker-controlled getters, Proxy traps, toJSON, or other traversal behavior.
security-reviewer.recommendedCorrection: Preserve bounded serialized text at the process boundary and add production-path oversized/adversarial coverage.

contract-auditor.exactClaim: Codebase Memory oversized-response evidence does not cover the production process transport path.

normalizedActiveFindings.rootCause: The Codebase Memory process transport has a pre-parse 200,000-byte line accumulator guard, but its final result-size contract is enforced only after JSON.parse(raw) and JSON.stringify(value.result); overflow rejects pending requests without terminating the child; and no production process-path regression proves the boundary.
normalizedActiveFindings.claimCorrection: The reserialization is real and redundant, but standard JSON.parse without a reviver creates inert JSON data. Arbitrary caller-supplied Proxy/getter/callable-toJSON/iterator execution is not reachable through the actual spawned-process path.

securityPreviousApprovalHistory.explanation: Revision 2 Security approved a different candidate before Revision 3 changed the host adapter and integration boundary files. Revision 3 used fresh current source evidence and inherited the same concrete transport reserialization concern raised by Code/Integration; it did not identify a newly introduced regression. Its executable-object wording is overstated for standard JSON.parse output, but its demand for a production-path bounded transport proof is materially valid. A fresh Security closure call remains required after the final transport correction.

codebaseMemoryTransportFlow.operation: When server-only config is enabled, CodebaseMemoryService is constructed with createProcessTransport(executable, workspaceRoot, timeoutMs).
Host-created JSON-RPC request is JSON.stringify-ed and written to stdin.
stdout Buffer chunks are decoded to UTF-8 text and appended to a newline-delimited string buffer.
Projected Buffer.byteLength(buffer)+Buffer.byteLength(text) is compared with CODEBASE_MEMORY_RAW_LINE_MAX_BYTES before append and parse.
A complete newline-delimited raw JSON-RPC line is removed from the buffer.
Standard JSON.parse(raw), with no reviver, creates value.
value.id and value.error are inspected; value.result is read only for a successful pending response.
JSON.stringify(value.result) produces the Promise<string> required by UpstreamTransport.
parseUpstreamResult checks string type and 200,000 UTF-8 bytes, then JSON.parse(raw) before normalization.
Normalized CodebaseMemoryResult is schema-bounded and cached/persisted after parsing.
Only adapter-bound serialized strings reach registeredOutputToToolResult; no non-test production caller of executeBoundToolOperation was found.
ToolResult is downstream and capped at 16,000 bytes; overflow does not call a provider/model.

processApi: Node child_process.spawn with shell:false; no exec/execFile/maxBuffer wrapper and no MCP transport library.
stdoutRepresentation: Buffer chunks from a spawned child, decoded to UTF-8 text, accumulated as newline-delimited JSON-RPC response text.
stderrRepresentation: A piped ChildProcess stderr stream is created but no listener, collection, redaction, or inclusion in Codebase Memory errors exists. It is not part of the returned result contract and is outside this final result-boundary correction.
stdoutBufferingBehavior: The current string buffer accumulates until newline and checks a projected 200,000 UTF-8-byte total on each stdout data event. The guard is before JSON.parse, but it measures the JSON-RPC line buffer rather than the result payload; after overflow it clears pending/buffer and returns without killing or pausing the child.

stdoutLimitBefore.measurement: Buffer.byteLength(decoded text, utf8) plus current string buffer byte length
stdoutLimitBefore.position: before append and before JSON.parse for the accumulated line

stdoutLimitAfterPlanned.measurement: Raw stdout Buffer bytes for the active newline-framed response plus bounded carry-over
stdoutLimitAfterPlanned.position: during stdout collection, before retaining over-limit data; overflow terminates the child and rejects pending calls

parseFunction: JSON.parse(raw) in the process stdout handler; service parseUpstreamResult(raw) calls JSON.parse(raw) again after its own string/byte guard.

parsedResultRuntimeSemantics.valueOrigin: Only standard JSON.parse(raw) over a child stdout line in the production process transport; no reviver or alternate parser.
parsedResultRuntimeSemantics.valueType: Ordinary JSON object/array/primitive with normal Object.prototype or Array.prototype semantics.
parsedResultRuntimeSemantics.valueResult: An ordinary JSON data value read from the parsed envelope; it cannot contain executable functions, accessors, Proxy identity, or custom iterator methods from serialized JSON alone.
parsedResultRuntimeSemantics.diagnostic: A safe local probe produced an own data __proto__ property, object-valued constructor/toJSON data properties, ordinary Object.prototype, and no Symbol.iterator.
parsedResultRuntimeSemantics.contentTrust: Still untrusted supplemental external content; inert does not mean trusted or authoritative.

arbitraryProxyProductionReachable.proof: The only production producer of value is standard JSON.parse(raw) in the private stdout listener; no production caller supplies value directly.

arbitraryGetterProductionReachable.proof: Standard JSON.parse creates data properties, not accessor descriptors; live-object injection exists only in test-level service dependency injection, not at the transport stringify site.

callableToJsonProductionReachable.proof: A toJSON JSON key is parsed as an ordinary data property, not a function; no transformation installs a callable method before value.result is stringified.

customIteratorProductionReachable.proof: JSON.parse does not create Symbol.iterator methods and the transport does not iterate value.result.

jsonStringifyLocation: src/integrations/codebase-memory/transport.ts:18, inside the successful JSON-RPC response branch after JSON.parse(raw) and value.result access.
jsonStringifyPurpose: Extract the JSON-RPC result field into the existing UpstreamTransport Promise<string> contract so CodebaseMemoryService can apply its bounded parse and normalization; it is not the generic ToolResult boundary, redaction, or primary byte limit.
jsonStringifyRiskClassification: Redundant parsed-JSON reserialization and late result-specific enforcement; executable-object risk is overstated for this real process path, but resource/lifecycle and producer/consumer evidence risk remain.
jsonStringifyFinalDisposition: KEEP_WITH_PROVEN_INERT_INPUT for this bounded closure. Do not introduce a custom parser or transport library; prove standard JSON.parse provenance and keep the existing string producer/consumer contract.
realProductionDefect: The process transport has a generic line guard before parse, but the final result guard is after envelope parse and result reserialization; overflow rejects pending requests without terminating the child; and the actual process path has no regression proving over-limit rejection, cleanup, and valid response continuity.
revisedRootCause: Codebase Memory's process transport receives newline-delimited JSON-RPC stdout, bounds the active line before JSON.parse, then reserializes the parsed result to satisfy the serialized UpstreamTransport contract before the service applies its result guard. Standard JSON.parse without a reviver makes value.result inert JSON data, so the remaining defect is a late result-specific bound, incomplete overflow cleanup, and producer/consumer evidence gap rather than arbitrary JavaScript execution from serialized process payloads.
context7CurrentState: Keep unchanged. Context7Transport is serialized text, has a 200,000-byte guard before parse/normalization/cache, and Revision 3 added a service-path oversized regression.
shadcnCurrentState: Keep unchanged. Official response.text() and injected transport are serialized text, have a 200,000-byte guard before parse/normalization/cache, and Revision 3 added a service-path oversized regression.
codebaseMemoryCurrentState: Keep service string contract, parseUpstreamResult guard, normalized cache/persistence ordering, and existing authority policies. Final closure targets only process stdout overflow lifecycle and production-path evidence.

preFixProof: Confirm spawn/piped stdout with no args/maxBuffer wrapper.
Confirm overflow rejects pending calls and clears buffer but does not kill/reset the child.
Confirm JSON.parse(raw) has no reviver and JSON.stringify(value.result) is reached only after parser-created value.
Confirm no non-test production caller injects a live object into the transport stringify site.
Confirm Context7/shadcn/generic Revision 3 evidence remains passing and unchanged.
correctionSteps: Keep CODEBASE_MEMORY_RAW_LINE_MAX_BYTES at 200,000 UTF-8 bytes and count raw stdout Buffer bytes for the active response before appending over-limit data.

On overflow, fail pending calls with the existing bounded CODEBASE_MEMORY_UNAVAILABLE error, clear pending/buffer, kill/terminate the child, reset the process reference, and stop parsing/retaining output.
Preserve standard JSON.parse(raw) and existing JSON.stringify(value.result) only as a proven-inert parsed-JSON-to-Promise<string> conversion.

Add a programmatic temporary child-process fixture through CodebaseMemoryProcessTransport or createProcessTransport that emits oversized newline-framed JSON-RPC output, proves rejection before parent JSON.parse/result handling, verifies child cleanup/no raw persistence, and proves a fresh valid bounded response.
Preserve cancellation isolation, read-only allowlist, current workspace/index checks, normalization, cache/persistence, UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL provenance, and existing Context7/shadcn/generic tests.

transportLimitPolicy.measurement: UTF-8 bytes from stdout Buffer chunks, not JavaScript character count
transportLimitPolicy.earliestBoundary: stdout data handler before appending to active response buffer and before JSON.parse
transportLimitPolicy.resultGuard: Existing CODEBASE_MEMORY_RAW_RESULT_MAX_BYTES 200,000 guard remains in service.parseUpstreamResult
transportLimitPolicy.genericToolResultGuard: Existing generic 200,000-byte serialized guard and 16,000-byte ToolResult bound remain separate
transportLimitPolicy.failure: Typed bounded unavailable error; no raw stdout in error text, cache, persistence, model prompt, or authority decision

overflowBehavior: Reject pending calls, clear pending and active buffer, terminate the child, reset process state, and do not parse, inspect value/result, stringify the result, normalize, cache, persist, log raw payload, or reach generic ToolResult/model stages.
processCleanupBehavior: Use the existing child.kill lifecycle; make overflow invoke it and clear the process reference so a later call starts a fresh child. Preserve exit-handler pending rejection and cancellation isolation.

The child is terminated/cleaned up on overflow and no raw payload is retained or logged.

Boundary-sized and multibyte UTF-8 fixtures demonstrate byte-based enforcement without a large static fixture.
